macOS builds are now signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple.

## What this changes

Downloading 2.0.0 on macOS produced this:

> Apple could not verify "GhostwrAIter" is free of malware that may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy.

That message was never about the contents of the application. macOS simply could not verify where it came from, because the build carried no Developer ID signature and had not been submitted to Apple for notarization. Working around it required a terminal command or a trip through System Settings.

2.0.1 is the same application as 2.0.0, signed and notarized. It opens on a double click, on your machine and on anyone else's.

## If you already installed 2.0.0

Download 2.0.1 and replace the application. Your drafts, strategy and calendar live outside the app bundle and are untouched.

## No other changes

No feature, fix or dependency differs from 2.0.0. See the [2.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/AutomatisIA/GhostwrAIter/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what that version brought: target audience selection end to end, the redesigned Library, the Antigravity engine, and the pinned CLI execution policy.
